Hi Amira / Ben —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our agreement on the call I’m attaching the Redwood redlines to the MSA and a draft security exhibit that clarifies audit rights and evidence cadence. Top asks from your side we want to validate:

- Scope limitation: we proposed limiting audit activities to ClearBridge-hosted systems that process Redwood-managed data (and a defined list of environments).

Subject: Re: Security exhibit: pen test window, SOC 2 evidence cadence, and MSA redlines for ClearBridge Health

Thanks Avery — quick notes from InfoSec and procurement:

1) Pen test window: we can accept a 7-day notice for non-intrusive scans, but ClearBridge requires a 48-hour interruption window notice for any intrusive tests. We also request a standard 2-hour emergency rollback point and a single-point-of-contact during the test. Can Redwood commit to those operational controls?

2) Evidence cadence: we appreciate the quarterly snapshots. For systems processing PHI (subset of the integration layer) we need at least monthly extracts or an automated SFTP feed for specific control logs.

3) Audit scope: we are okay limiting auditor access to the in-scope systems. However, our legal team wants stronger language excluding personnel interviews and on-site interviews without a court order or separate written consent.

I’ve looped in Ben (legal) and procurement. Ben — can you review the attached redlines and flag any exposure on indemnity or broad 'audit' definitions?

Best,
Amira Khan
Director, Information Security
ClearBridge Health

Avery / team —

Thanks — reviewed Amira’s note. High level: we should accept the operational requests with tighter contractual guardrails. My suggested approach (summary):

- Pen test language: accept 48-hour notice for intrusive tests, require mutual coordination SLA (we propose Redwood to provide POC and notification, CB to provide maintenance window and suppression rules). Insert a mandatory Nondisruptive clause: tests must not materially impact availability or patient flows; Redwood reserves right to pause tests on detection of production impact.

- Evidence cadence: propose a split schedule: quarterly control snapshots (policy/config, control evidence) + monthly log extracts for systems that are explicitly listed as PHI-scoped. We’ll add a table (Evidence_Cadence_Table_ClearBridge.xlsx) listing the data feeds and transfer method (SFTP with per-file encryption).

- Audit rights: limit to automated evidence pulls and SOC 2 reports. For on-site interviews or hands-on access, require a separate scoping agreement and 30-day prior written approval; exclude personnel interviews in the base SOW.

- Indemnity: we need to avoid open-ended indemnities tied to security incidents outside Redwood control. Recommend a carve-out for third-party vendor breaches and a liability cap tied to the order form.

I pasted a redline snippet below for the security exhibit — please use if it helps when replying to Amira.

--- redline snippet (suggested wording) ---
Security Exhibit, Section 3 (Audit & Evidence):
"Customer may request copies of Redwood’s applicable SOC 2 Type II report(s) and related control documentation. Redwood will provide quarterly control snapshots and, for systems in the PHI-scoped list, monthly log extracts. Any on-site audits or personnel interviews require a separate, mutually-agreed scoping agreement and 30 days' prior written notice. Penetration testing that could materially impact availability will require a minimum 48 hours' notice and Redwood reserves the right to suspend testing upon detection of production impact. Evidence delivery will be via encrypted SFTP or a mutually-agreed secure transfer mechanism."

--- end snippet ---

I’ll prepare a v2 of the security exhibit incorporating the above and circulate. Marissa / Laura — please confirm whether the proposed SFTP + per-file encryption meets our operational controls.

Karthik
General Counsel (acting)
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Security exhibit: pen test window, SOC 2 evidence cadence, and MSA redlines for ClearBridge Health

Quick operational confirmation:

- SFTP with PGP per-file encryption is fine for the evidence cadence. We should also include a retention window for snapshots (e.g., 90 days for logs, 12 months for control artifacts) and an SLA for evidence requests (Redwood will turn around non-sensitive control artifacts within 5 business days; forensic or sensitive logs within 10 business days).

- For pen tests: Redwood can provide a named POC and support during the test window; we should add a requirement that the customer indicate the specific IP ranges and test vectors in advance. That avoids vague 'all systems' testing.

- On-site audits: as Karthik suggested, require separate scoping, signed agreement, and reasonable limits on duration (max 3 business days) with costs borne by the requesting party unless otherwise agreed.

I’ll review the v2 when it lands. From a CS/ops standpoint, this is workable if the PHI-scoped list is finalized before signature.

—Laura
Director, Security Assurance
Redwood Inference

Amira / Ben —

Thanks for the quick review and the clear asks. We updated the security exhibit to reflect the team’s feedback and attached Security_Exhibit_ClearBridge_v2_20260911.pdf (redline to follow in the portal). Summary of agreed points below for clarity:

- Pen test: Redwood accepts 48-hour notice for intrusive tests, 7-day notice for non-intrusive scans. Customer will provide IP ranges and test vectors in advance; Redwood will provide a named POC and may pause tests if production impact is observed.
- Evidence cadence: Quarterly control snapshots for all scoped systems; monthly log extracts for PHI-scoped components. Delivery via encrypted SFTP, per-file PGP. Retention windows: logs 90 days, control artifacts 12 months. Redwood SLAs: 5 business days for non-sensitive artifacts, 10 business days for sensitive/forensic logs.
- Audit scope: Base audit rights limited to SOC 2 report access and evidence deliveries. On-site audits or personnel interviews require a separate scoping agreement, 30 days' prior written notice, and reasonable cost allocation (requesting party).
- Indemnity & liability: Redwood proposes a liability cap and carve-outs for third-party vendor incidents — see v2 redline.

Next steps: Attached is the v2 exhibit and the redlined MSA for your legal team. If that looks good, I included a DocuSign link for the order form and exhibit: https://docusign.com/link/clearbridge-rdwd-20260911. If you need any amendments to the PHI-scoped list, please send the list by EOD Monday and we’ll incorporate into the SOW.

Thanks again — happy to jump on a 30-minute call early next week to finalize.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
